answer: Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a anchor index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Because the beacon index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the meadow audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 193 aliases thus needs 193 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
